dimensions.label: Income consistency
dimensions.about: How steady your income is from month to month. Swing means how far a typical month is from your average month. A full score needs a swing of 15% or less; the score is zero at 100% or more.
dimensions.measure: Your monthly income swung 30% around its average of USD 1,833 over 12 months.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, make your months more even. At a swing of 15% or less you get all 25 points; yours is 30%.
steps: No payment is recorded in 1 of your 12 full months. If you were paid in any of them, record the payment; until you do, they count as months with no income.
Your weakest month, June 2026, has no payment recorded, against USD 2,000 in a typical month. A typical month there would raise this area. This is worth about 4 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Profit margin
dimensions.about: How much of what you earn is left after the business expenses you recorded. A full score needs 60% or more left; the score is zero at 0% or less. Only expenses recorded in LanceraOS count. Personal spending and savings are not tracked here.
dimensions.measure: You kept 45% of your income: USD 22,000 received, USD 12,100 spent, USD 9,900 left.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, keep more of your income. When 60% or more is left you get all 20 points; you kept 45%.
steps: Your expenses were 55% of your income (USD 12,100 against USD 22,000). Your largest group was Platform and payment fees at USD 3,025. Spending USD 2,200 less (10% of your income) would raise this area. This is worth about 3 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Tax compliance
dimensions.about: Whether your tax basics are in place: an NTN saved (8 points), a PSEB registration number saved (4 points), a payment recorded in the last 90 days (4 points) and an expense recorded in the last 90 days (4 points). The NTN and PSEB number are what you entered; LanceraOS does not check them with FBR or PSEB. PSEB registration is for people who export IT services, so it may not apply to your work.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, complete the missing checks: PSEB number saved.
steps: If you have a PSEB registration number, save it in Settings, then Tax & PSEB. PSEB registration is for people who export IT services, so it may not apply to your work. This is worth about 4 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Income growth
dimensions.about: How your average month compares with your average month in the same number of months before it. A full score needs growth of 30% or more, flat income earns half the points, and a fall of 30% or more scores zero.
dimensions.measure: Your average month was USD 1,833 over the last 12 months, against USD 2,000 over the 6 months before (down 8%).
dimensions.needed: To score higher, grow your average month. At growth of 30% or more you get all 20 points; yours is down 8%.
steps: Your average month was USD 1,833 over the last 12 months, against USD 2,000 over the 6 months before. An average month of USD 2,200 (10% above the earlier months) would raise this area. This is worth about 6 points of your score.

dimensions.label: Client diversity
dimensions.about: How much of your income depends on one payer, using the "Received from" name on your payments. A full score needs your biggest payer to be 30% or less of your named income; the score is zero at 80% or more. This needs a name on at least 70% of your income.
dimensions.measure: Big Corp paid 60% of the income that has a name (USD 13,200 of USD 22,000). You have 3 named payers.
dimensions.needed: To score higher, spread your income across more payers. When your biggest payer is 30% or less you get all 15 points; yours is 60%.
steps: Big Corp paid 60% of the income that has a name (USD 13,200 of USD 22,000). If your biggest payer were 50% of it, that would raise this area. This is worth about 3 points of your score.
